newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spanish minister fights for his honour in Congress.
newsitem.headline: Spanish minister fights for his honour in Congress.

text.p: Spain's Defence Minister Eduardo Serra faced Congress on Wednesday to defend his honour after a series of press reports last week accused him of graft.
The minister told the congressional defence commission that honesty had been "the guiding principle of my entire life".

The charges that Serra headed a construction firm that paid illegal commissions were published in the daily El Mundo, which has played a major role in revealing scandals that brought 13 years of Socialist rule to an end.

Serra said the chairmanship of the company, Cubiertas, was offered to him in 1991, when the irregular payments were already public knowledge and he made it a condition of his acceptance that the practice be ended.
"I intended that the said practice cease for personal reasons and because the company was losing competitiveness," the minister said.
He also denied having made any contact with the then-Civil Guard chief Luis Roldan, accused by El Mundo of receiving $1 million in bribes from Cubiertas in return for construction contracts.
El Mundo also alleged that Serra had interceded on behalf of a brother-in-law in 1986 for a contract from the paramilitary Civil Guard.
"I've never had the even the most minimal personal or professional contact with Roldan," Serra said.

The minister, an independent who has few friends in the conservative Popular Party (PP) government, has been supported against the corruption charges by Prime Minister Jose Maria Aznar, although other PP deputies have called for his resignation.

The parliamentary groups on the defence commission said they were satisfied with Serra's explanations, except for the United Left coalition which said the most prudent move would be for the minister to offer his resignation.
The charges against Serra were the first to hit Aznar's government, which had pitched a "clean hands" election campaign to a public weary of hearing of political scandals.
